questions.question: In the pattern 13; 20; 27; 34 each term is found by:
options: Adding 7 to the previous term — a constant difference
Adding a growing amount each time

questions.question: The pattern 5; 10; 20; 40 belongs to which family?
options: Constant ratio — each term is multiplied by 2

questions.question: The pattern 1; 3; 6; 10 has steps of 2, then 3, then 4. It is called:
options: A growing-step pattern — the steps themselves change with their own rule

questions.question: Consecutive terms means:
options: Terms standing next to each other in the list
The first and last terms only

subtopics.title: The Difference Row — Your First Test

questions.question: The difference-row test means:
options: Dividing each term by the one before
Writing the difference between each pair of consecutive terms and checking whether it is constant
Counting how many terms there are

questions.question: In the list 13; 20; ___; 34 with a constant difference of 7, the missing term is:
options: 27 — reached as 20 plus 7 and confirmed as 34 minus 7

questions.question: A courier charges R13 for the first kilometre and R7 for each extra kilometre. Seven kilometres cost:
Why must the answer be written as R55 rather than 55?
options: The exam answers in the story's units — money answers carry the rand sign
Rand signs make answers look longer
The memo ignores numbers without letters

questions.question: For 5; 10; 20; 40, dividing each term by the one before gives:
The next term after 40 in the pattern 5; 10; 20; 40 is:
The key contrast between the first two families is:
options: Constant difference grows by the same factor; constant ratio by the same amount
Both grow by the same amount each step
Constant difference grows by the same amount each step; constant ratio by the same factor

questions.question: Asked which pattern grows faster in the long run, the reasoning mark is earned by saying:
options: The multiplying pattern wins eventually, though the adding pattern may lead at first
The adding pattern always stays ahead

subtopics.title: Growing Patterns and the Stacked-Rows Question

questions.question: Rows hold 1; 2; 3; 4; 5; 6; 7 circles. The running totals 1; 3; 6; 10; 15; 21; 28 are called:
options: Triangular numbers — the totals of stacked rows

questions.question: The difference row of the totals 1; 3; 6; 10; 15; 21; 28 is:
The pairing check for 1 up to 7 works as:
options: Three pairs of 8 plus the middle 4, giving 24 plus 4 which is 28

questions.question: A decoration has seven rows built this way. The biggest mark-loser is answering:
options: 7 when the question asked for the total of 28 circles
28 when the question asked for the total
With a table instead of a formula

questions.question: The staircase picture describes a constant difference pattern because:
options: Staircases get steeper as you climb
Every step lifts you by the same amount, so climbing is repeated adding

questions.question: For a missing middle term, the both-sides walk means:
options: Adding the step from the term before AND subtracting it from the term after, trusting only agreement

questions.question: The minibus zones cost 13; 20; 27; 34 rand. The step is:

subtopics.title: The Pattern That Doubles Like a Rumour

questions.question: The rumour reaches 5; 10; 20; 40 people hour by hour. The multiplier is caught by:
options: Dividing each hour's number by the hour before — always 2
Adding the first and last hours

questions.question: The rumour starts behind the staircase pattern but overtakes it because:
options: Doubling compounds — same factor each step beats same amount each step eventually

questions.question: The test order to run under pressure is:
options: Subtract neighbours first; if gaps are not equal, divide neighbours to hunt a constant ratio

subtopics.title: Cans at the Shop and the Growing Step

questions.question: In the can pyramid, the gaps between running totals grow by one each time because:
options: Cans keep falling off the stack
The shop adds two rows at a time
Every new row is one can longer than the row above it

questions.question: The running-total method for seven rows lands on:
options: 28 cans, built one small addition at a time

questions.question: Why is the two-column table a safe exam method for growing patterns?
options: Every line is one small addition the marker can follow, so nerves cannot derail it

questions.question: The seventh row holds 7 cans but the display holds 28. The lesson is:
options: Rows and stacks are the same thing
Always answer with the bigger number
Read whether the question counts one row or the whole stack before answering
